newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-No need to merge now, OUB says.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-No need to merge now, OUB says.

text.p: Overseas Union Bank Ltd sees no need at present to consider a merger with another bank, president and chief executive officer Peter Seah said on Friday.
Seah said OUB, one of Singapore's four main banks with total assets at the end of 1995 of Singapore $25.63 billion, had grown rapidly over the last five years.

It was now the fifth largest bank in ASEAN after the other three Singapore banks -- The Development Bank of Singapore Ltd, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp and United Overseas Bank Ltd -- and Thailand's Bangkok Bank, he said.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
"We have done very well, not just increasing our capital size but in using the capital," Seah told Reuters in an interview.
"So there should be no pressures for us to want to merge with anybody in the foreseeable future."
Seah said conditions may change, making it necessary for the bank to reconsider its position.
"If you look down the road, it is very difficult to say... As the business environment changes, should the need arise, that could be something that has to be reviewed," he said.
He said whenever people talked of banking mergers with reference to OUB, it was always in the context of OUB merging with another Singapore bank.
But, if the need for a merger arose, OUB could also choose to look further afield for a partner.

"We are not just a Singapore orientated organisation. There is nothing to prevent us from merging with banks in other countries or to bring in a joint venture partner from other countries," Seah said.
"When the environment changes, there are a lot of other options. But at the moment, I would say there is definitely no need (for a merger) and it is strictly an academic discussion."
Seah said OUB was constantly on the look-out for opportunities to access a market either on its own or in terms of a joint venture or an acquisition.

"But our basic requirement is in whatever we do in all these markets, we want to have management control. In other words we want to be responsible for guiding the destiny of whatever business or company we go into," he said.
